### Proposal drafted by

Founder, Action State

### Proposed working group name

Attestation & Evidence Working Group (AE-WG)

### One-sentence summary (elevator pitch)

Make the actions, decisions, authorizations and outcomes of AI agents independently verifiable: define how statements about them are attested, how those attestations become evidence that survives across organizational boundaries, how evidence is graded, held, disclosed and composed, and how a party who was not present can check it without a central authority.

### Detailed description of the working group's focus and scope

### Attestation & Evidence Working Group (AE-WG):
Initial Draft Charter (will change) 
Type: cross-working-group, with a liaison seat from every AAIF WG. 

Co-chairs: TBD. 
Term: one year, elected by AAIF TC

### Mission
Make the actions, decisions, authorizations and outcomes of AI agents independently verifiable: define how statements about them are attested, how those attestations become evidence that survives across organizational boundaries, how evidence is graded, held, disclosed and composed, and how a party who was not present can check it without a central authority.

### Why now
Every AAIF WG produces or consumes evidence about agents, and none owns what makes it checkable later. Identity & Trust gives who; Observability & Traceability gives what was observed; Workflows gives the engine's record. Governance needs evidence classes to map onto obligations, Accuracy & Reliability needs an evidence base to evaluate against, Agentic Commerce needs settlement and dispute evidence, Security & Privacy reviews all of it. Independence of the reviewer and independence of the record are different properties; this WG addresses the second.

### Goals

- Bilateral and multi-party attestation: each side of a consequential interaction seals its own observation; agreement and disagreement are derived, never asserted.
- Portable, requestable evidence bundles: self-describing, verifiable offline; a request yields an artifact, a signed refusal, or a recorded absence; bundles declare their own completeness and disclosure boundary.
- A clear taxonomy of witnesses and roots of trust (logs, cosigners, timestamp authorities, TEE, HSM, secure element / NFC, organizational), each mapped to what it establishes.
- Shared understanding across the WGs and the ecosystem.

### Scope
In: evidence vocabulary and classes; attestation of actions, decisions, authorizations and outcomes; commitment before the question; multi-party evidence at boundaries; disclosure and requests; composition and verification; mapping to obligations with GRR.

Out: identity and credentials (I&T); telemetry formats (OT); evaluation and verdicts (A&R); threat models (S&P); payment operations (AC); regulatory interpretation (GRR); hardware attestation mechanisms themselves; certification of systems; any foundation-operated ledger.

### Principles
Coordinate first, specify only where a gap is shown, upstream where a venue exists. Evidence is interoperable; judgment stays plural. Commitment establishes properties of records, not truth about the world. No central authority. Vendor neutrality; implementations named by project only. Reuse the siblings' use cases, architectures and taxonomies rather than rewriting them.

### Commitments: the first 90 days

- Month 1: charter ratified with deliverable and timelines; repo and channels; one liaison per sibling WG; Evidence Vocabulary v0 (siblings' terms adopted, plus the evidence-class scale).
- Month 2: an evidence column on each sibling WG's existing use cases; witness and root-of-trust table v0; a two-page standards delta.
- Month 3: Evidence Classes and Gap Analysis 1.0, with an adopt / extend / specify recommendation per gap, for a TC vote; one page of evidence requirements per sibling WG.
- At the 90-day review the WG re-charters for Layer 2 (profiles of existing artifacts as AAIF Community Specifications, conformance vectors, controls mapping with GRR and CSA) and later Layer 3 (composition, judgment binding, primer, conformance-program recommendation), or converts to a liaison workstream.
- 

### How it works
Rough consensus, co-chair-led resolution, one vote per organization as fallback, TC as escalation. Weekly 30-minute open meeting offset from OT and I&T; minutes in the repo; Discord and Slack.

Roles at start: two co-chairs, a GitHub maintainer (not a chair), seven liaisons. Seated as the work arrives: cryptography and legal reviewers, a privacy reviewer from S&P, an assurance review panel from more than one audit firm, research, frontier-lab and evaluator liaisons. Apache-2.0 code, CC-BY-4.0 documents, DCO, LF antitrust guidelines, LF Code of Conduct.

### Relationships and coordination
Inside AAIF: liaison from each WG; MCP, Goose, A2A as proving grounds; Taxonomy & Landscape for vocabulary.

Outside: Adv AI Society / CNCF / CCC (patterns reused), OpenSSF, CSA (controls mapping), OWASP, ISO/IEC SC 42 and CEN JTC 21 through GRR, LF Decentralized Trust's Proof-of-Control lab (shared vocabulary, liaison offered), NIST, AICPA / IAASB as the assurance panel's references, IETF WGs (primitives upstreamed).
Neutrality and conflicts
Members participate as individuals. No deliverable advantages a vendor, product or project. Individual Internet-Drafts are inputs on equal footing, with IPR status recorded.

Disclosure: Steven Mih authors drafts in this space, maintains open source implementations of those drafts and runs a company that will offer independent witness-related services; he recuses himself from adopt / extend / specify decisions on any gap where he is an author, and no deliverable names his company or his company's commercial products or services.
